hspy-01-c1.text: Sun Tzu; Lionel Giles (trans.) (1910). The Art of War. The Internet Classics Archive (MIT).
hspy-01-c1.quote: Now this foreknowledge cannot be elicited from spirits; it cannot be obtained inductively from experience, nor by any deductive calculation.
hspy-01-c1.claim: It cannot be drawn from spirits, or worked out from experience or calculation: knowledge of the enemy's dispositions can only be obtained from other men.

hspy-01-c2.text: Joshua J. Mark (2020). Arthashastra. World History Encyclopedia.
hspy-01-c2.quote: The work was considered lost, its existence only known through references to it in later pieces, until it was discovered by Shamasastry in 1905 CE.
hspy-01-c2.claim: The work was known only from later references until the Sanskrit scholar Rudrapatna Shamasastry found a copy in 1905.

hspy-01-c3.text: David Magie (trans.) (1921). Historia Augusta: The Life of Hadrian. LacusCurtius, University of Chicago.
hspy-01-c3.quote: The frumentarii, at first petty-officers connected with the commissary of the army, became, probably under Trajan, couriers charged with the conveyance of military dispatches
hspy-01-c3.claim: Probably under Trajan, around the turn of the second century CE, they became couriers carrying military dispatches.

hspy-02-c1.text: The National Archives. Teaching resource: Elizabeth I’s monarchy, part one. The National Archives.
hspy-02-c1.quote: Thomas Cely, from Bristol, was one of Elizabeth’s Yeomen of the Guard and most probably also a spy for the queen.
hspy-02-c1.claim: Thomas Cely, one of Elizabeth's Yeomen of the Guard and most probably also a spy, wrote to her in 1579 as a galley slave of the Spanish Inquisition, after being put to the rack.

hspy-02-c2.text: Alan Bryson (2022). The Gallows Letter. British Library, Medieval manuscripts blog.
hspy-02-c2.quote: These letters were intercepted, unsealed, and deciphered by Phelippes, before being resealed and carried to their intended addressee.
hspy-02-c2.claim: In this way Walsingham read all of Mary's correspondence.

hspy-02-c3.text: Harrison W. Mark (2025). The Violent and Mysterious Death of Christopher Marlowe. World History Encyclopedia.
hspy-02-c3.quote: Poley and Skeres were experienced agents who had helped uncover the 1586 Babington Plot to assassinate the queen.
hspy-02-c3.claim: The coroner's papers, found only in 1925, show he was in the company of Robert Poley and Nicholas Skeres, experienced agents who had helped uncover the Babington Plot.

hspy-03-c1.text: Yale News (2026). ‘Unfurling the Flag’ at the Beinecke Library. Yale News.
hspy-03-c1.quote: While no contemporary sources confirm that he spoke those words, in the public’s mind, his stoic sacrifice made him a model patriot.
hspy-03-c1.claim: Witness accounts agree that he met his death with composure and a firm resolve, but no contemporary source confirms that he spoke those words.

hspy-03-c2.text: The Culper Ring. American Eras (Gale), via Encyclopedia.com.
hspy-03-c2.quote: Washington had a high opinion of the Culpers but never met either man.

hspy-03-c3.text: The Culper Ring. American Eras (Gale), via Encyclopedia.com.
hspy-03-c3.quote: The code could have been easily broken but fortunately this never occurred.
hspy-03-c3.claim: The code could have been easily broken, but it never was.

hspy-04-c1.text: The National Archives. Intelligence and security services. The National Archives research guides.
hspy-04-c1.quote: there are, confusingly, no records generated by the agency held at The National Archives
hspy-04-c1.claim: MI6 has not: confusingly, the archive's own guide notes that no records generated by the agency are held there.

hspy-04-c2.text: Imperial War Museums. Spies, Lies and Deception Large Print Guide. Imperial War Museums.
hspy-04-c2.quote: So, when Roos telegraphed an order from Edinburgh for 10,000 Sumatra S.S. cigars on 25 May 1915, he meant that there were ten battleships in Edinburgh.
hspy-04-c2.claim: Their price list was a code in which each cigar type meant a kind of warship, so when Roos ordered 10,000 Sumatra cigars from Edinburgh, he meant that ten battleships were in port there.

hspy-04-c3.text: Imperial War Museums (2017). Revamping the Vamp: Mata Hari Myths and Realities. Imperial War Museums, First World War Centenary Partnership.
hspy-04-c3.quote: After her execution by the French in October 1917, she was held responsible for the deaths of 50,000 Allied men and was portrayed as an immoral woman who traded sex for classified intelligence.
hspy-04-c3.claim: Afterwards she was held responsible for the deaths of 50,000 Allied soldiers and portrayed as a seductress who traded sex for secrets.

hspy-05-c1.text: The National Archives. MI5: Official Secrets. The National Archives.
hspy-05-c1.quote: The evidence that Josef Jakobs, the last person executed at the Tower of London, was a German spy.
hspy-05-c1.claim: Some were unsuitable and were executed, and one of them, Josef Jakobs, was the last person executed at the Tower of London.

hspy-05-c2.text: Walter Wolf III (2020). Secret Agents, Secret Armies: The D-Day Misfit Spies. The National WWII Museum.
hspy-05-c2.quote: Pujol only made it as far as Lisbon, but there he began to concoct “intelligence” derived from public sources and attributed to a network of fictitious sub-agents.
hspy-05-c2.claim: He got only as far as Lisbon.

hspy-05-c3.text: Commonwealth War Graves Commission (2022). The Man Who Never Was: The True Story of Operation Mincemeat. CWGC blog.
hspy-05-c3.quote: German signals intercepted by the Government Code and Cypher School (GC&CS) showed Operation Mincemeat had worked so well that even four hours after the invasion began, 21 Axis aircraft left Sicily to reinforce Sardinia.
hspy-05-c3.claim: Even four hours after the invasion of Sicily began on 9 July, 21 Axis aircraft left Sicily to reinforce Sardinia.

hspy-06-c1.text: Robert Louis Benson, Michael Warner (eds.) (1996). Venona: Soviet Espionage and the American Response, 1939-1957. NSA and CIA (Center for the Study of Intelligence).
hspy-06-c1.quote: the KGB's cryptographic center in the Soviet Union for some unknown reason printed duplicate copies of the "key" on more than 35,000 pages of additive and then assembled and bound these in one-time pads.
hspy-06-c1.claim: For a few months in early 1942, a time of great strain for the Soviet regime, the KGB's own cryptographic centre printed duplicate copies of the key on more than 35,000 pages and bound them into separate pads, so supposedly unique pages existed twice.

hspy-06-c2.text: Atomic Heritage Foundation. The Rosenberg Trial. Nuclear Museum (Atomic Heritage Foundation).
hspy-06-c2.quote: The documents suggest his involvement was with military and industrial espionage, rather than atomic espionage, as previously believed.
hspy-06-c2.claim: Venona confirms that Julius (LIBERAL) led a productive spy ring, though the decrypts suggest his main work was military and industrial espionage rather than atomic secrets.

hspy-06-c3.text: Mark Dunton, Chloe Lee, Gill Bennett (2025). On the Record: MI5: Official Secrets. The National Archives.
hspy-06-c3.quote: They kidnapped Volkov and his wife drugged them, took them to Moscow, brutally interrogated them, and then executed them.
hspy-06-c3.claim: He tipped off Moscow, and Volkov and his wife were kidnapped, drugged, taken to Moscow, interrogated and executed.

hspy-07-c1.text: Central Intelligence Agency. The Berlin Tunnel. CIA Museum.
hspy-07-c1.quote: Subsequent studies determined that the Soviets had not attempted to feed false information over the tapped lines
hspy-07-c1.claim: Soviet propaganda implied so, but later CIA studies concluded the intelligence was genuine.

hspy-07-c2.text: Central Intelligence Agency. CORONA: America's First Imaging Satellite Program. CIA Museum.
hspy-07-c2.quote: This remarkable technological achievement revolutionized the intelligence world by returning from space more photographic coverage of the Soviet Union in a single mission than in all previous U-2 missions combined.
hspy-07-c2.claim: On 18 August 1960 Mission XIV worked, and it returned more photographic coverage of the Soviet Union than all previous U-2 missions combined.

hspy-07-c3.text: Benjamin B. Fischer (1997). A Cold War Conundrum: The 1983 Soviet War Scare. CIA Center for the Study of Intelligence.
hspy-07-c3.quote: The Soviets' intelligence "failure" of 1941 was a failure of analysis, not collection.
hspy-07-c3.claim: The failure was one of analysis, not collection.
